triggers.grounds: The matched word 'paragraphing' names the MASORETIC parashah layer, not translation punctuation, WEB paragraphing, quotation structure or any other tier-4 metadata: the row writes 'a petuchah (single-witness, tier-3 corroboration) in the Masoretic paragraphing at oshb:Eccl.1.11'. The mark is real and correctly typed - the byte-extracted inventory carries exactly 4 segs (1 PE at MT 1:11 plus 3 SAMEKH at MT 3:1, 3:8, 9:10) and MT 1:11 is the PE, so no PE/SAMEKH conflation; the marks checker returns 0 flags and 0 warns over this row, and the row repeats the single-witness tier-3 label inside boundary_evidence_refs. It carries CORROBORATION weight only, on a close independently warranted by tier-1 bytes standing in the cited verses' own text: the governing question at oshb:Eccl.1.3 and the closing memory verdict at oshb:Eccl.1.11 both re-collate at BYTE tier, and no independent-pronoun restart stands anywhere inside 1:3-1:11 (sweep ani: 25 verses book-wide, none of them in 1:3-1:11; nearest sites 1:12 and 1:16), the row's sole first-person trace being the 1cp suffix at oshb:Eccl.1.10 (byte tier). Per the book law the Writings parashah layer is legitimate tier-3 weak corroboration, so this is a retro-scan false positive for the PUNCT lane, not a tier-4 driver or tier-4 corroboration.

findings.claim: The cross-seam refrain disclosure misstates where the tachat-hashemesh refrain resumes: it places web:Eccl.1.14 'one verse past this row's own 1:11|1:12 seam' when 1:14 stands three verses past that seam.
findings.grounds: Sweep tachat-hashemesh (skeleton, VERSE count): 27 verses book-wide, ch 1 = 3 verses - 1:3, 1:9, 1:14 - which confirms both the row's in-span sites and its own 'ch.1 count: 3' digit. The two verses that actually follow the seam carry no tachat-hashemesh at all: 1:12 carries none, and 1:13 carries the DIFFERENT formula תַּ֣חַת הַשָּׁמָ֑יִם (oshb:Eccl.1.13, byte tier, 'under the heavens'), so no charitable reading makes the resumption one verse past the seam - even counting 1:13's sibling formula would give two. The cited ref (web:Eccl.1.14) is right, the digit is right, the ref is mirrored in boundary_evidence_refs, and the disclosure is device_notes texture rather than a seam warrant, so the defect is confined to the distance descriptor.
findings.proposed_change: device_notes field repair only: replace 'one verse past this row's own 1:11|1:12 seam' with 'three verses past this row's own 1:11|1:12 seam', or drop the distance and keep 'at the next site, web:Eccl.1.14'. No other field, ref, span or confidence is affected.

triggers.grounds: TEST 1 (register law): 'the natan-plus-lev construction that opened the preceding row at 1:13' sits in boundary_rationale, a driver field; the book's register purge bars positional row references outright and requires cross-row references to be verse-anchored. TEST 2 (E-18 arm): the reference carries an argumentative claim about another row, and re-derived from bytes that claim is FALSE - the preceding row's span is Eccl.1.12-Eccl.1.15 and its opening verse is 1:12, אֲנִ֣י קֹהֶ֗לֶת הָיִ֥יתִי מֶ֛לֶךְ (oshb:Eccl.1.12, byte tier); the natan-plus-lev construction וְנָתַ֣תִּי אֶת לִבִּ֗י (oshb:Eccl.1.13, byte tier) stands at 1:13, that row's SECOND verse, and the neighbour row's own prose calls 1:13 the point where the row 'continues into the first wisdom inquiry'. The claim is not load-bearing: the seam warrant is the dibbarti verb at 1:16 (sweep: 2 verses book-wide, 1:16 and 2:15 - re-swept and confirmed), so the lane test yields medium, recorded as the matching finding below.

findings.class: E-06 register bleed carrying a byte-false cross-row claim (E-18 arm)
findings.claim: The rival-defeating disclosure asserts that the natan-plus-lev construction 'opened the preceding row at 1:13'; 1:13 is that row's second verse, not its opening, and the assertion contradicts the neighbour row's own account of 1:13.
findings.grounds: The preceding row's span Eccl.1.12-Eccl.1.15 opens at 1:12 with אֲנִ֣י קֹהֶ֗לֶת הָיִ֥יתִי מֶ֛לֶךְ (oshb:Eccl.1.12, byte tier); וְנָתַ֣תִּי אֶת לִבִּ֗י stands at 1:13 (oshb:Eccl.1.13, byte tier). The substantive recurrence the sentence exists to disclose is TRUE and survives the repair: וְנָתַ֣תִּי אֶת לִבִּ֗י (oshb:Eccl.1.13, byte tier) and וָאֶתְּנָ֤ה לִבִּי֙ לָדַ֣עַת (oshb:Eccl.1.17, byte tier) are both natan-root plus lev, so the row's 'disclosed here rather than implied absent' posture is honest and only the positional attribution is defective. Not load-bearing - the restart driver is the dibbarti verb (sweep: 2 verses, 1:16 and 2:15), which the row cites with its digit.
findings.proposed_change: boundary_rationale field repair: drop the positional row reference and the false 'opened' attribution, re-anchoring on the verse alone (e.g. 'the natan-plus-lev construction standing at 1:13 ... recurs inside this row at 1:17'). Span, refs, unit_type and confidence unaffected.

findings.class: byte-false comparative in a disclosure field
findings.claim: device_notes contrasts 1:18's hevel-free close with 'the quest units on either side of it', but neither flanking unit closes on a hevel token.
findings.grounds: Sweep hevel (skeleton, VERSE count): 30 verses book-wide. The row's own span 1:16-1:18 carries none - that half of the claim is byte-true. But the flanking units' CLOSING verses carry none either: 1:15 (close of Eccl.1.12-Eccl.1.15) and 2:2 (close of Eccl.2.1-Eccl.2.2) are both absent from the 30-verse list, their hevel tokens standing mid-unit at 1:14 and 2:1. Under the sentence's dominant reading, fixed by its own gloss 'a bare gnomic conclusion rather than a vanity-formula close', the contrast is byte-false on both sides; under the weaker reading ('unlike those units, which carry hevel somewhere') it is true, so the finding is held at low. Not load-bearing: device_notes texture, and the seam rests on the dibbarti verb.
findings.proposed_change: device_notes field repair: state the true contrast - this row's whole span carries no hevel-family token while the flanking units carry theirs mid-unit at 1:14 and 2:1 - and drop the 'vanity-formula close' comparison.

triggers.grounds: The band is honest and the stated reason is byte-real. The span is 8 verses of a 26-verse chapter, so no whole-chapter cap applies. Both outer seams rest on tier-1 lexical signals standing in their own verses' bytes: תַּ֣רְתִּי בְלִבִּ֔י (oshb:Eccl.2.3, byte tier) opens the row, and the turning formula opens 2:11 as the row says. The honest source of the reduced band is disclosed in the row's own prose - MT 2:4 opens asyndetically, which the row concedes is 'a genuine clause break' inside its span - so the confidence is neither over-stated (it masks no byte-defective warrant: every Hebrew splice in the row re-collates at BYTE tier and the citation, mark, refs-mirror, WEB-quote and language-zone checkers all return GREEN) nor dishonestly under-stated. The separate defect in the rival-rejection warrant is recorded as a finding below rather than as a mis-banded confidence.

TEST 1 (register law): 'before a fresh turning-formula opens the next row at 2:11' is a positional row reference in boundary_rationale, which the register purge bars. TEST 2 (E-18 arm): the reference is verse-anchored and its substantive claim is byte-TRUE - 2:11 does open on the turning formula (the neighbour row quotes it from 2:11's own bytes at BYTE tier, and web:Eccl.2.11 is mirrored in this row's boundary_evidence_refs). A true claim merely phrased in workflow register scores low; recorded as the matching finding below.

findings.class: rival-rejection warrant does not cross the contested seam
findings.claim: The rival 'split the works catalogue from its wine-test introduction (2:3)' is rejected on cohesion evidence lying entirely inside 2:4-2:9, which says nothing about the contested 2:3|2:4 seam.
findings.grounds: The row concedes the seam marker - 'MT 2:4 opens asyndetically ... a genuine clause break' - and then rejects the split 'on the lexical cohesion the ethical dative li and the mikol...lifnay...bi-Yerushalaim inclusio supply across web:Eccl.2.4-Eccl.2.9'. Re-derived from bytes, both cited objects stop short of the seam. Word-bound li per verse (skeleton token count, word-bound rather than substring, since a contiguous li sweep also returns amali-type tokens): 2:3 = 0, 2:4 = 2, 2:5 = 1, 2:6 = 1, 2:7 = 2, 2:8 = 2, 2:9 = 1, 2:10 = 0 - the run is real and unbroken over exactly 2:4-2:9 (6 verses, matching the row's digit) but does not touch 2:3 at all. The phrase inclusio is likewise confined to the same stretch (sweep lifnay-birushalaim: 2 verses, 2:7 and 2:9). Neither object bears on why 2:3 belongs with 2:4-2:10, so the warrant offered does not defeat the rival it is aimed at. Not alone load-bearing: the row's outer seams are independently warranted (tarti at 2:3, the turning formula at 2:11), and the embedded neighbour row supplies the cross-seam reading this rationale omits by treating 2:3 as the opening of one wine-building-accumulation experiment.
findings.proposed_change: strongest_rejected_alternative / boundary_rationale field repair: replace the rejection ground with one that actually crosses 2:3|2:4 (e.g. the single first-person experiment frame opened at 2:3 whose self-benefit clauses 2:4-2:9 execute), or state plainly that the 2:3|2:4 clause break is conceded and the unit is held together on the experiment frame. No respan proposed - the span itself is not challenged.

findings.class: E-05 count-object blending (grammatical class labelled over a token sweep)
findings.claim: 'the ethical dative li ... (sweep: 6 verses)' attaches a grammatical-function label to a digit true only of the bare token; two of the six instances are not ethical datives.
findings.grounds: Word-bound li stands in all six verses 2:4-2:9 (per-verse counts above), so the DIGIT and the extent are byte-true. The function is not uniform: 2:7 carries the existential-possessive הָ֣יָה לִ֑י (oshb:Eccl.2.7, byte tier, 'there was to me') twice, and 2:9 carries the stative עָ֥מְדָה לִּֽי (oshb:Eccl.2.9, byte tier, 'remained with me') - neither is the reflexive-benefactive ethical dative of 2:4, 2:5, 2:6 and 2:8. The book's semantic-class count discipline requires the swept object to be named first (spelling vs term vs formula vs construction) and bars blended objects. The cohesion substance survives a correct relabelling, so this is held at low.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: name the swept object as the word-bound li token ('sweep: 6 verses, 2:4-2:9, word-bound') and, if the ethical-dative function is to be argued, restrict it to 2:4, 2:5, 2:6 and 2:8.

findings.claim: boundary_rationale carries the positional row reference 'before a fresh turning-formula opens the next row at 2:11', barred by the register purge even though the claim itself is verse-anchored and byte-true.
findings.grounds: Register law: row prose describes the text, never the process, and cross-row references are verse-anchored. The substantive claim re-derives true (the turning formula stands in 2:11's own bytes and web:Eccl.2.11 is mirrored in boundary_evidence_refs), so the defect is cosmetic register only.
findings.proposed_change: boundary_rationale field repair: replace 'opens the next row at 2:11' with a verse-anchored form such as 'before the turning formula at 2:11 opens a fresh movement'.

findings.class: frontier-queue gap at a low-band row (book strategy sidecar rule)
findings.claim: The row ships at medium_low with frontier_flag_considered = false, although the book's strategy requires a frontier-queue row for every low-band chunk.
findings.grounds: The owner-ruled strategy's low-confidence section mirrors every medium_low/low decision into all three sidecars and adds a frontier-queue row for EVERY low-band chunk. This is the only low-band row in the batch with the flag false: the other three low-band rows audited here (Eccl.3.19-Eccl.3.21 at medium_low, Eccl.4.9-Eccl.4.12 at medium_low, Eccl.4.13-Eccl.4.16 at low) all carry frontier_flag_considered = true, so this is an internal inconsistency against the writer's own pattern and against a rule in force at the book's close, not a later convention. Mechanical field-level defect only; no byte claim, seam or span is affected.
findings.proposed_change: Field repair: set frontier_flag_considered = true and confirm the row is mirrored in the frontier queue with the other low-band chunks.

triggers.grounds: TEST 1 (register law): 'opens the animal-comparison the following row develops' is a positional row reference in boundary_rationale and is NOT verse-anchored - it names no verse for the following unit - which the register purge bars twice over. TEST 2 (E-18 arm): the substantive claim re-derives TRUE - 3:18 does open the animal comparison (its own bytes carry the behemah catchword) and the next unit, Eccl.3.19-Eccl.3.21, develops it (behemah recurs in 3:19 and 3:21). A true claim in workflow register scores low; recorded as the matching finding below. Everything else in the row survives adversarial re-derivation: both self-address splices re-collate at BYTE tier at their own refs, and the 'identical' claim in strongest_rejected_alternative holds at the STRICTEST tier - the opening three words of MT 3:17 and MT 3:18 are byte-identical to each other, so the unnamed tier is an understatement rather than an overclaim; both verses also carry the definite ha-elohim form as device_notes states, and no YHWH token exists anywhere in the book (sweep: 0).

findings.class: E-06 register bleed (positional row reference, not verse-anchored)
findings.claim: boundary_rationale closes on 'opens the animal-comparison the following row develops', a positional row reference with no verse anchor.
findings.grounds: Register law: row prose describes the text, never the process, and cross-row references must be verse-anchored. The underlying claim is byte-true (behemah stands in 3:18's own bytes and recurs at 3:19 and 3:21) and web:Eccl.3.18 is in boundary_evidence_refs, so the defect is cosmetic register only. Independent checks over this row are clean: citation sweep, marks, refs-mirror, WEB-quote and language-zone checkers all GREEN, and every Hebrew splice re-collates at BYTE tier.
findings.proposed_change: boundary_rationale field repair: re-anchor on the verse, e.g. 'opens the animal-comparison carried on from 3:19'.

triggers.grounds: Well-calibrated and honestly reasoned. The span is 3 verses, so no whole-chapter cap is in play. The genuine weakness is the row's own opening: 3:19 begins on a causal subordinate clause dependent on the behemah catchword already standing in 3:18's bytes - and the row states exactly that, in those terms, rather than concealing it, and carries frontier_flag_considered = true. The seam is nevertheless defensible: 3:18 closes a complete predication and 3:19's ki-clause opens an extended reflection, so this is not the mid-clause cut that the book's syntactically-continuous-single-sentence rule would force into one unit. The embedded neighbour row agrees the argument straddles the seam and discloses it too, so the two rows are coherent rather than incompatible. Confidence is neither over-stated (no byte-defective warrant is masked: every Hebrew splice re-collates at BYTE tier and all Tier-0 checkers are GREEN over this row) nor dishonestly under-stated.

findings.proposed_change: boundary_rationale field repair: 'before the distinct raiti formula at 3:22 opens its own verdict'.

findings.class: prose referent defect in a driver field (correct ref, wrong antecedent)
findings.claim: '...into the dust-return statement of 3:20, closing that same verse on [ki hakol hevel] (oshb:Eccl.3.19)' attaches 'that same verse' to 3:20, which is neither where the quoted clause stands nor how 3:20 closes.
findings.grounds: MT 3:19 does close on the quoted hakol-hevel clause and the cited ref oshb:Eccl.3.19 is correct and re-collates at BYTE tier, so the citation saves the claim. But the nearest antecedent in the sentence is 3:20, and MT 3:20 closes instead on וְהַכֹּ֖ל שָׁ֥ב אֶל הֶעָפָֽר (oshb:Eccl.3.20, byte tier); the sentence also runs the argument forward into 3:20 and then back to a clause standing before it. A reader taking the plain antecedent would derive a byte-false statement about 3:20. The hakol-hevel digit itself is correct (sweep: 6 verses book-wide - 1:2, 1:14, 2:11, 2:17, 3:19, 12:8).
findings.proposed_change: boundary_rationale field repair: name the verse explicitly ('closing 3:19 itself on ...') and order that clause before the move into 3:20.

findings.class: undisclosed count object on a corroborating device claim
findings.claim: The who-knows closural argument cites a single comparandum (web:Eccl.2.19) with no sweep digit, while the formula stands at four verses book-wide, two of them undisclosed and inside the same monologue.
findings.grounds: Sweep mi-yodea (skeleton, VERSE count): 4 verses - 2:19, 3:21, 6:12, 8:1. All four sit inside the monologue parent, and at 6:12 and 8:1 the formula is not closural, which weakens the 'treated consistently here' generalisation the row builds from one other site. The row's factual claims about 2:19 are true (it carries the formula, waw-prefixed, with the wise-or-fool alternatives the row contrasts against 3:21's unanswered question), and no exclusivity word is used, so this is a disclosure shortfall against the book's own '(sweep: N verses)' convention rather than a false claim. Not load-bearing: the 3:21|3:22 seam is independently warranted by the byte-true raiti restart at 3:22. Whether 2:19 closes a row in the shipped corpus is not verifiable from the auditor's named path set and is not counted against the row.
findings.proposed_change: boundary_rationale field repair: add the digit and the object ('the who-knows formula, sweep: 4 verses book-wide') and disclose the two non-closural sites, or drop the consistency generalisation and rest the close on 3:22's raiti restart alone.

triggers.grounds: The band is appropriate and its stated reason is honest. The span is 4 verses, so no whole-chapter cap applies. The declared reason for the low band is the unit_type deviation - wisdom_poem applied inside a parent whose operative default is monologue_unit - which the operative-category law permits precisely with the one-sentence deviation disclosure the row supplies, plus the cross-seam ordinal echo the row weighs against itself. Both supporting byte facts re-derive TRUE: 4:9-4:12 carry no first-person verb, and the three lead particles are genuinely distinct (ki-im at 4:10, gam-im at 4:11, ve-im at 4:12, each re-collating at BYTE tier at its own ref), so the form argument the deviation rests on is sound. The confidence masks no byte-defective warrant and is if anything conservative, since the unit's edges are strong in the bytes. The separate warrant defect below is recorded as a finding, not as a mis-banded confidence.

findings.class: seam warrant absent from the driver field / deferred to a boundary 'already established'
findings.claim: The row states no affirmative byte warrant for either of its own seams: the opening seam is deferred to a boundary 'already established' by the preceding unit's shavti restart at 4:7, which warrants that unit's opening rather than the 4:8|4:9 seam, while two byte warrants standing at the seam itself go uncited.
findings.grounds: boundary_rationale offers only continuity ('answers the solitary toiler of 4:8'), the unit's shape and its closing quotation; the only boundary-relevant byte evidence in the row - no first-person verb, the three-particle conditional run - sits in strongest_rejected_alternative as a unit_type argument, and device_notes then defers the seam to 'the independent shavti-restart boundary already established at web:Eccl.4.7-Eccl.4.8|Eccl.4.9'. The shavti restart stands in 4:7, i.e. it establishes the PRECEDING unit's opening (sweep shavti/veshavti: 3 verses - 4:1, 4:7, 9:11), and the preceding row as embedded likewise argues its own opening and 4:8's content but never its close. Two byte warrants at the seam are available and uncited: 4:8 closes on the verdict גַּם זֶ֥ה הֶ֛בֶל וְעִנְיַ֥ן רָ֖ע הֽוּא (oshb:Eccl.4.8, byte tier), a closural refrain, and 4:9 opens on the comparative טוֹבִ֥ים הַשְּׁנַ֖יִם מִן הָאֶחָ֑ד (oshb:Eccl.4.9, byte tier) - a genuine tov-min construction with an intervening token, which is why it escapes the contiguous tov-min adjacency sweep and must be checked as a construction. Not alone load-bearing: the span itself is not challenged and the form evidence in the rival field is byte-true.
findings.proposed_change: boundary_rationale field repair: state the row's own seam warrant from the seam's own bytes (4:8's closural hevel verdict and 4:9's tov-min comparative opener) and move the form evidence out of the unit_type rival into the boundary case. No respan proposed.

findings.claim: device_notes calls the 'no second' construction the content of 'this row's own opening verse'; it stands at 4:10, the row's second verse.
findings.grounds: The row's span opens at 4:9, whose bytes are טוֹבִ֥ים הַשְּׁנַ֖יִם מִן הָאֶחָ֑ד ... (oshb:Eccl.4.9, byte tier) and contain no ordinal 'no second' clause. Sweep ein-sheni (skeleton, VERSE count): 2 verses - 4:8 and 4:10 - which confirms both the row's 2-site exclusivity claim and its digit; the cited ref (oshb:Eccl.4.10) is correct and re-collates at BYTE tier, as does the 4:8 comparandum at its own ref, and the ketiv/qere disclosure is correct too, since 4:8's K/Q variant stands later in the verse than the quoted span. Only the 'opening verse' descriptor is false, and the disclosure is device_notes texture.
findings.proposed_change: device_notes field repair: 'this row's second verse' (or 'the row's own 4:10') in place of 'this row's own opening verse'.

triggers.grounds: A well-calibrated low-band row with sound grounds - CLEAN. The low band is expressly sanctioned by the book's own low-confidence law, which names 4:13-16 (the two-youths passage - referential ambiguity, rayon-ruach close) as an expected low-confidence region, and the row carries frontier_flag_considered = true with a bespoke, non-boilerplate uncertainty statement. The stated reason for the band is byte-honest: the referents of the two figures are genuinely not named in the row's bytes. The seams and the internal case re-derive TRUE against the bytes: 4:13 opens on a tov comparative and 4:16 closes on the hevel plus rayon-ruach verdict, both re-collating at BYTE tier at their own refs; rayon-ruach is correctly counted and correctly kept distinct from reut-ruach (sweep rayon-ruach: 2 verses - 1:17 and 4:16 - matching the row's digit, while reut-ruach is a different attested form at 7 verses); 4:15's verse-initial asyndetic raiti is real, and the row raises it AGAINST its own convenience before overriding it on the anaphoric chain from the indefinite yeled at 4:13 to the definite ha-yeled ha-sheni at 4:15, which is byte-true (4:14 introduces no yeled). The comparanda hold: 3:22 and 4:4 both carry waw-prefixed raiti in their own bytes, and 3:22 is the driver of the embedded neighbour row. The row writes no ch-5 ref, so the offset-zone dual-cite rule is not engaged, and every Tier-0 checker (citation sweep, marks, refs-mirror, WEB quotes, universals, language zones) returns GREEN over it. Confidence is not over-stated; the residual uncertainty is interpretive rather than boundary-level, but the band is exactly what the book's law prescribes here.
